what_was_tried: Fetched PWPW's own news item 'PWPW wins in Greece' (pwpw.pl/m/en/News/2023/06/pwpw-wins-in-greece.html), 19 June 2023.
result: Dead. The contract is for the production and supply of PASSPORT PAPER for the Central Bank of Greece, not banknotes. No banknote printer stated.

target: PWPW foreign customer sweep (pwpw.pl export results page)
what_was_tried: Fetched 'The value of PWPW exports doubled in 2018' (pwpw.pl/en/News/2019/01/...) and the Polish trade piece bank.pl/?p=263697 (5 Oct 2018), which together enumerate PWPW's foreign customers.
result: No new printer records. Banknote customers named are Guatemala (Banco de Guatemala), Honduras, Dominican Republic and Paraguay - all four already have records. Everything else named is non-banknote: Iceland (passports and e-cards), Ecuador (passport components), Georgia and Cyprus (digital tachographs), Armenia, Azerbaijan and Lithuania (tachographs, e-ID cards), Turkey, France, Portugal (products not specified). The PWPW vein appears exhausted for banknotes: the same four Latin American customers recur across every page.

what_was_tried: Both the PWPW 2018 export page and bank.pl name 'produkcja banknotu kolekcjonerskiego dla Dzibuti' (production of a collector banknote for Djibouti).
result: Not filed. The source states only a single COLLECTOR banknote, names no issuing bank or central bank, and gives no date. It does not state that PWPW prints Djibouti's circulating banknotes.

target: Lesotho (LSO) and Morocco - G+D per-country case-study/press vein
what_was_tried: Fetched G+D press release 'Based on G+D technology, banknotes from Lesotho and Morocco honored as Regional Banknote of the Year' (07/03/2024).
result: Dead as a printer record. G+D says only that the notes were 'produced or equipped with security features by G+D' without saying which applied to which note. For Lesotho's 200 maloti (Central Bank of Lesotho) it describes substrate, PET film, mineral-oil-free inks and a Louisenthal RollingStar i+ thread; the printer is not named. For Morocco's 100 dirham it describes only a Louisenthal thread and watermark. Neither supports 'prints'.

what_was_tried: Searched gi-de.com case studies, customer stories and insights pages for central bank banknote work.
result: The case studies that surfaced are cash-management software, not printing: 'Compass System Intelligence at the National Bank of Belgium', Compass Banknote Intelligence, BPS X9 inspection at Banque de France, a cash centre for Banco Nacional de Angola, and currency processing for Malawi. None states that G+D prints that country's banknotes. This vein yields equipment and software contracts, not printer records.

what_was_tried: Fetched Narodna banka Slovenska's 'Euro banknotes production' page (nbs.sk/en/banknotes-and-coins/legal-framework/euro-banknotes-production/).
result: Dead. The page lists only legal instruments, including a guideline on 'the establishment of the Eurosystem Production and Procurement System'. It names no printing works or firm. Consistent with the earlier finding for Italy, Greece, the Netherlands, Belgium and Ireland.

target: Saudi Arabia (SAU) - SAMA's own works, first attempt
what_was_tried: Fetched Saudipedia's 'Saudi Currency' article.
result: Insufficient on its own: it says the 1959 monetary law 'centralized the printing, minting, and issuance of Saudi currency under SAMA' but does not say whether SAMA printed the notes itself. The record for SAU was filed from the Tunisie Numerique piece instead, which names the Saudi Central Bank Printing Works.

target: Uruguay (URY) - own works or named printer
what_was_tried: Attempted to fetch the Banco Central del Uruguay banknotes and coins page (bcu.gub.uy/Billetes-Monedas/Paginas/Inicio.aspx).
result: Could not be fetched - bcu.gub.uy is robots-disallowed. No alternative third-party source naming Uruguay's printer surfaced; the search returned only BCU budget decrees and digital-banknote pilot coverage. URY needs a third-party source in a later round.

target: Venezuela (VEN) - Casa de la Moneda del BCV as a state works
what_was_tried: Attempted to fetch LaPatilla's 'Colapsada la Casa de la Moneda del BCV por impresion acelerada de billetes de Bs. 100' (10 June 2015).
result: Could not be fetched (site client error). The BCV's own Casa de la Moneda in Maracay therefore remains unrecorded as a state works; the VEN record filed is the Goznak contract instead. A working source for the Maracay works is still needed.

what_was_tried: Searched for the Central Bank of Myanmar's state security printing works and attempted to fetch The Irrawaddy's 'Cash-strapped Myanmar regime in money printing frenzy'.
result: Could not be fetched (site client error). No other source surfaced that names Myanmar's printing works. Unresolved.

what_was_tried: Searched for a Bank of the Lao PDR printing factory and fetched Keesing Technologies' 'Laos issues new 10,000 kip and 20,000 kip banknotes' (8 November 2022).
result: Dead. The page credits only the issuer - 'The Bank of the Lao People's Democratic Republic issued upgraded 10,000 Kip and 20,000 Kip banknotes in late October 2022' - and names no printing works or firm.

what_was_tried: Fetched PrintWeek's 'De La Rue to print new Iraqi currency' (undated, internally consistent with July 2003).
result: Dead. The article says De La Rue was only 'poised to win the main contract to produce banknotes for Iraq', that no formal contract had been signed and negotiations were at an early stage. It names no ordering bank or authority, no denominations and no volume. An intention is not a contract, so nothing was filed.

what_was_tried: Fetched Central Banking's 'Uganda gives banknotes a facelift' (4 May 2010).
result: Dead. The body text covers the launch of the USh2,000 note and the redesigned denominations but never says who printed them. De La Rue appears only in the page's organisation/keyword metadata ('De La Rue, Bank of Uganda'), which does not state the fact.

what_was_tried: Fetched Landqart's 'Central Bank of the Bahamas releases new $100 note'.
result: Not filed. Landqart names its own Durasafe substrate and thanks 'the other partners in this endeavour who have come together to create this beautiful banknote: Canadian Bank Note Company, Limited, Crane Currency, Orell Fussli Ltd. Security Printing, and SICPA' - but assigns no role to any of them, so none can be stated as the printer. The page is also undated ('today'). A near-miss worth revisiting with a Central Bank of the Bahamas source.

target: Israel (ISR) - Bank of Israel's own currency pages
what_was_tried: Fetched the Bank of Israel's 'Second Series of the New Sheqel' page (boi.org.il/en/economic-roles/banknotes-and-coins/second-series-nis/).
result: Dead. The page gives dimensions, security features and the designers (Naomi Rosner and Meir Eshel) but never mentions a printing company, Israeli or foreign.

what_was_tried: Searched for a Bank of Mongolia statement or printer attribution for the tugrik notes.
result: Nothing usable. Search returned only Numista and Numisquare collector catalogue entries, no central bank or trade-press statement naming a printer. Not fetched; a crowd-edited collector database was judged too weak to file from. Unresolved.

what_was_tried: Searched for where National Bank of the Republic of Belarus ruble notes are printed.
result: Nothing usable. Search returned only collector catalogue listings (Numista, Numisquare, banknotes.com) and a reform.news piece about a new 200-ruble note's signature. No source naming a printer. Unresolved.

what_was_tried: Searched in Spanish and English for who prints Banco Central de Cuba peso notes and whether Cuba runs its own works.
result: Nothing usable. Search returned OnCuba and Central Banking coverage of new denominations plus collector listings; none named a printer or a Cuban works. Unresolved.

target: De La Rue press-release archive and 'Going Beyond' newsletter
what_was_tried: Searched for De La Rue press releases and contract awards naming individual issuing banks.
result: Partly productive but mostly off-target for the needs list. What surfaced named Bank of England (already recorded), Denmark (already recorded; a July 2026 currency-news item reports De La Rue won the new Danish series), Kenya and Tanzania (already recorded) and Libya (excluded as a known foreign-printing case). No 'Going Beyond' newsletter issue surfaced in search at all.

what_was_tried: Searched for Crane Currency contract announcements naming central banks.
result: No new needs-list records. The items that surfaced were the Caribbean guilder supply deal with the Royal Canadian Mint (Curacao/Sint Maarten, both already recorded), the Crane-Bank of Morocco joint venture to print notes for third countries (Morocco already recorded, no customer named), a Liberia item and Central Banking award write-ups. Crane does not appear to publish per-country launch releases at the rate De La Rue does.

target: Euro-area untried banks (FIN, SVN, EST, LVA, LTU, CYP, MLT, HRV, LUX)
what_was_tried: Searched the ECB's banknote-production and manufacturer-accreditation pages plus the NBS Slovakia page as a representative test of whether an NCB names the works that prints its allocation.
result: No records. The ECB pages describe the Eurosystem Production and Procurement System and the accreditation regime without mapping a printer to a country, and the one NCB page tested (Slovakia) names no producer. Given Italy, Greece, the Netherlands, Belgium and Ireland had already come back empty, and Slovakia makes six, this whole euro-area vein looks structurally closed: euro production is pooled and NCBs do not publish their printer. The remaining eight were not individually fetched.

target: Afghanistan (AFG) - weak aggregator source, discarded in favour of a better one
what_was_tried: Fetched mriguide.com/afghanistan-banknotes-to-be-printed-in-poland.
result: Discarded as the source: it names no central bank, carries no publication date, attributes a 'Polish National Procurement Authority' as the contracting party (implausible) and credits ToloNews second-hand. BanknoteNews was used for the AFG record instead because it gives the dated ToloNews attribution, names Da Afghanistan Bank and reports the 380 million delivery.
